qualifying_findings.title: Loop engineering framed as the enforceable runtime layer for agents
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: TrueFoundry describes an agent harness loop as the runtime place where persistence, context compaction, tool approvals, sandboxing, deferred capability discovery, and failure reconstruction are enforced between model calls.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a useful downstream-practice signal that high-risk coding-agent behavior should be enforced in the harness loop rather than expressed only as prompt guidance. It maps directly to local leaves on harness components, lifecycle hooks, context rehydration, and approval controls.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, consider whether application-patterns should connect loop-level enforcement to existing leaves for harness components, session recovery, lifecycle hooks, structured outputs, and MCP approval evidence.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Do not create a local TrueFoundry or TrueForge product leaf; route product background upstream.

qualifying_findings.title: Structured outputs require schema, deterministic validation, and authorization layers
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: TrueFoundry separates free-form text, valid JSON, schema-conforming objects, business-valid objects, and authorized actions; it notes that JSON mode is not a stable contract and that tool-call schemas still need policy enforcement.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The source reinforces the local pattern that model-drafted artifacts and tool calls need layered validation. It adds a concise practice distinction between syntactic parsing, schema conformance, business invariants, and authorization gates.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, strengthen structured-output guidance around schema portability limits, provider refusal/truncation handling, deterministic domain validators, and authorization after validation.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Keep provider-specific feature details upstream or source-attributed; local wiki should own the validation contract practice.

qualifying_findings.title: Stateful MCP human approval distinguished from binary allow/deny controls
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: TrueFoundry argues that MCP human-in-the-loop approval needs a stateful gateway workflow that persists pending requests, notifies authorized approvers, records decisions, and issues scoped expiring grants.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This adds a clear practice requirement for approval evidence: approval gates should record who approved what payload, for which scope, under what expiry, instead of treating MCP policy as only a per-request ACL.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, compare with mcp-scoped-authorization-and-approval-evidence.md and governance-controls-for-agents.md for approval package fields and gateway state requirements.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Treat the TrueFoundry versus Kong product comparison as upstream-owned and vendor-attributed; keep only the approval-state pattern locally.

qualifying_findings.title: AI code review economics should measure false-positive triage cost
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Faros argues that the economic cost of AI code review depends on reviewer triage time from false positives, not only model or tool price, and gives an example where ten minutes of human triage exceeds the apparent per-request price difference.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local wiki already tracks agent cost telemetry and code-review rubrics; this source adds a practice metric for AI review selection: precision and downstream reviewer time should be measured as part of total review cost.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, consider adding review false-positive triage time to code-review evals and agent-cost telemetry as a measurable adoption cost.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Source is vendor analysis; avoid adopting its numeric example as universal.

qualifying_findings.title: Versioned review standards presented as repo-owned agent skills
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: DevOps.com reports that Tessl Code Review stores review standards as team-owned, versioned skill files in the repository and evaluates pull requests using the surrounding codebase, team standards, and thread discussion rather than only the diff.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a local practice signal for durable review instructions: review criteria should be inspectable, versioned with source, and applied against codebase context rather than hidden inside a vendor system.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, evaluate whether intelligent-code-review.md and durable-instructions-and-skill-files.md should mention repo-owned review standards as a reviewability and portability pattern.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Do not create a Tessl product page locally; retain only the versioned-review-standard practice.

qualifying_findings.title: Pull requests reframed as evidence carriers for agent-generated changes
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: CodeRabbit argues that pull requests carry more context when agents produce code: generated changes need independent validation, prioritization by consequence, guided change explanations, and human accountability before shipping.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The source reinforces local fix-branch, PR packaging, and review-gate guidance: when author reasoning is weak or absent, the PR should carry evidence, risk triage, tests, and ownership decisions.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, map this to source-workflows and coding-practices leaves that treat PRs as accountable evidence bundles rather than simple diffs.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Vendor product features should stay attributed; local content should focus on PR evidence requirements.

qualifying_findings.title: AI code factories increase demand for verification pipelines
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: QA Wolf argues that AI-assisted code generation has increased production velocity faster than verification capacity; it distinguishes line coverage from user-flow verification and calls for testing pipelines that scale with agent output.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This directly supports local verification-tax and AI-assisted TDD themes: agent throughput should not be counted as productivity unless verification, E2E coverage, flake handling, and feedback loops scale with it.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, consider adding verification capacity as an adoption bottleneck metric for coding-agent programs.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Vendor framing is opinionated; use as supporting practice evidence, not as universal incident data.

qualifying_findings.title: Database agents framed around pre-approved reports rather than free SQL generation
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Oracle describes letting agents use durable memory and query enterprise data through Oracle AI Database and MCP, with the article explicitly inviting discussion about pre-approved reports as an alternative to agents generating their own SQL.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This adds a concrete governed-data-agent pattern: expose bounded, pre-approved data tools and reports rather than direct arbitrary query generation when agents need enterprise data.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, route broad Oracle and MCP-server background upstream while keeping the local practice note that retrieval/data tools should prefer bounded reports, role-scoped queries, and audit evidence.

qualifying_findings.title: Platform-specific coding-agent skills used as guardrails for prototype generation
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Box describes using an AI coding agent with a Box Skill so prototype generation can rely on platform-specific workflows, guardrails, and verification steps rather than only general model knowledge.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This supports the local pattern that durable, portable skills should package platform constraints, guardrails, and verification procedures for coding agents working around external services.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, consider linking this to durable-instructions-and-skill-files.md and portable-agent-skills-and-runbooks.md as an example of platform-specific guardrail packaging.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Product and connector details belong upstream; local coverage should stay about skill packaging and verification boundaries.

qualifying_findings.title: Coding-agent orchestration described as one governed process artifact
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: UiPath announced Maestro Flow as a developer-first orchestration canvas that lets builders use supported coding agents to design, run, observe, and govern an end-to-end business process as a single artifact from environments such as VS Code or UiPath Studio.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a local practice signal for file-oriented enterprise builder workflows and process-layer state: agent-generated workflow work should become reviewable, observable, governed artifacts rather than disconnected prototype steps.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, compare with application-patterns/ai-process-layer-and-workflow-state.md and file-oriented-enterprise-builder-workflows.md for artifact review, observation, and governance requirements.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Because this is a press release, source claims should remain attributed.

qualifying_findings.title: Collaborative coding-agent channels make intermediate work observable
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: AI/TLDR summarizes Slack Code as a workflow that creates a dedicated channel for a coding-agent job, with conversation, plan, diffs, preview, high-stakes approval routing, archival, and searchability.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Although Slack Code is product/entity news, the local practice implication is strong: agent progress should be visible to the team before PR handoff, with high-stakes changes routed to named approvers and the run left as searchable evidence.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, map the practice to supervised handoffs, user-visible progress, runtime telemetry, and approval-boundary pages without duplicating Slack product coverage.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Prefer primary Slack source if available during ingest; this collector records the public digest signal because it has a visible in-window date and concrete workflow details.

qualifying_findings.title: Agent adoption metrics highlight coordination overhead from increased PR volume
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: AIToolsRecap reports on Linear aggregate workspace data, saying AI-authored issues rose toward half of issue creation, teams using coding agents increased weekly PR counts from 21 to 65, and total product development time still increased.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a practice-level adoption signal that agent output volume can increase coordination, triage, and review load instead of reducing cycle time unless operating agreements and verification capacity change.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: During ingest, consider agent adoption metrics that distinguish throughput from cycle-time improvement and include coordination burden in operating-model guidance.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Verify against the primary Linear report during ingest before treating numeric details as authoritative.
